mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2.5% year-over-year signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL YoY > 2.5%, or if the correlation between CPIAUCSL YoY and 20-day forward returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in Real Final Sales (RSAFS) indicates weakening consumer demand, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances where RSAFS declines for 3 consecutive months, or if the correlation between RSAFS 3-month change and 60-day forward returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in a month signals labor market weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of instances where UNRATE increases > 0.5% in a month, or if the correlation between UNRATE monthly change and 5-day forward returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in Industrial Production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a month signals strengthening supply-side fundamentals, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of instances where INDPRO increases > 1% in a month, or if the correlation between INDPRO monthly change and 20-day forward returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) is rising, the combination signals a tightening monetary policy with inflationary pressure, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL YoY > 2%, or if the joint effect of FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL on 60-day forward returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in Housing Starts (HOUST) signals strengthening demand in the housing market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of instances where HOUST increases for 3 consecutive months, or if the correlation between HOUST 3-month change and 20-day forward returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4% and Nonfarm Payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month, the combination signals a tight labor market with strong job growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
regime_hint: tight labor market with job growth
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 40% of instances where UNRATE < 4% and PAYEMS increases > 200,000, or if the joint effect of UNRATE and PAYEMS on 5-day forward returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, a decrease in GDP (GDPC1) by more than 0.5% quarter-over-quarter signals a weakening economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances where GDPC1 declines > 0.5% QoQ during a tightening cycle, or if the correlation between GDPC1 QoQ change and 60-day forward returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during tightening cycles.
